name: Nestle

rows.label: Revenue
rows.source: Nestle Nigeria Plc unaudited statement of profit or loss for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, NGN thousands: revenue 976,529,533, cost of sales 583,665,533, gross profit 392,864,000, other income 1,036,620, marketing and distribution 148,386,824, administrative 37,243,981, impairment 55,988, results from operating activities 208,213,827, finance income 37,136,441, finance costs 51,469,176, net finance costs 14,332,735, profit before income tax 193,881,092, income tax 90,507,040, profit 103,374,052, basic earnings per share 130.41 naira. Operating Expenses is marketing and distribution plus administrative expenses. The printed operating result of 208,213,827 is 980,632 above gross profit less those two expense lines, the difference being other income less the impairment charge, lines the panel does not render.

source_note: Gap fill 2026-11-12: Q3 2026 column added from the company unaudited nine month accounts filed with the NGX on 29 October 2026. Revenue 976,529,533 less cost of sales 583,665,533 equals the printed gross profit of 392,864,000, and profit before tax 193,881,092 less income tax 90,507,040 equals the printed profit of 103,374,052. | earlier note: H1 2026 column rebuilt 2026-10-06 from the issuer H1 2026 interim statement (Nestle Nigeria Plc unaudited interim financial statements for the six months ended 30 June 2026, filed on NGX): Revenue 650,759,475,000; Cost of Sales 392,238,873,000; Gross Profit 258,520,603,000; Operating Profit (EBIT) 141,363,719,000 (printed as Results from operating activities); Net Finance Costs 14,595,641,000 (finance costs 47.86bn less finance income 33.26bn); Profit Before Tax 126,768,078,000; Income Tax 61,991,246,000 (Profit Before Tax less Net Profit); Net Profit 64,776,832,000; EPS 81.72. UNIT: NGN. Prior H1 2026 cell set was wrong: Cost of Sales had been back-filled as Revenue minus Net Profit and Gross Profit, Operating Profit and Profit Before Tax had all been set to the Net Profit figure. Identities checked: Revenue minus Cost of Sales = Gross Profit; Profit Before Tax minus Income Tax = Net Profit.
derivedCellsNote: Individual blank cells derived from the same file own printed inputs, each tagged derived true with its formula and identity agreement rate.
